title: Premiere of Watch Mr. Wizard
phrase: the premiere of Watch Mr. Wizard
description: Don Herbert played a science hobbyist whose young neighbor dropped by every Saturday morning for an experiment. It went out live from Chicago's WNBQ, ran 547 live broadcasts until 1965, and won a Peabody Award in 1953.

title: MTV launches
phrase: the launch of MTV
description: The first video was, of course, "Video Killed the Radio Star" by the Buggles. In its first years MTV featured very few Black artists, until Michael Jackson's "Billie Jean" broke the color barrier the channel had put up.

title: Premiere of The Mysterious Cities of Gold
phrase: the premiere of The Mysterious Cities of Gold
description: A Japanese and French cartoon in which Esteban, Zia, and Tao cross the 16th-century Americas looking for the Seven Cities of Gold. Zia is the daughter of an Incan high priest, kidnapped by the Spanish invaders. It first aired on NHK in Japan and reached Nickelodeon in 1986.

title: Premiere of The Third Eye
phrase: the premiere of The Third Eye
description: Nickelodeon's anthology of spooky British and New Zealand serials, starting with Into the Labyrinth, The Haunting of Cassie Palmer, and Under the Mountain. Children of the Stones, about a village built inside a stone circle, joined in April.

title: Premiere of Mr. Wizard's World
phrase: the premiere of Mr. Wizard's World
description: Don Herbert brought Mr. Wizard back on Nickelodeon in a faster version of his 1950s show, filmed in Calgary and aired three times a week. Reruns kept going on Nickelodeon until 2000.

title: Premiere of Liquid Television
phrase: the premiere of Liquid Television
description: MTV's showcase of experimental animation, produced by Colossal Pictures. It introduced Æon Flux and Beavis and Butt-Head, who got their own show in 1993.

title: Premiere of The Real World
phrase: the premiere of The Real World
description: Seven strangers in a New York loft, filmed for three months. Mary-Ellis Bunim and Jonathan Murray had pitched MTV a scripted soap, and when that cost too much they tried an unscripted one. Reviews were mostly negative, and it ran until 2017.

title: Premiere of Avatar: The Last Airbender
phrase: the premiere of Avatar: The Last Airbender
description: Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko's Nickelodeon series about Aang, the last airbender, who has to master all four elements to end a hundred-year war. It ran three seasons, until July 2008, and won a Peabody Award.

title: Character Will Byers disappears in Stranger Things
phrase: Will Byers (the character) vanishing into the Upside Down
description: Twelve-year-old Will goes missing in Hawkins, Indiana, and his mother Joyce, his brother Jonathan, and police chief Jim Hopper start a town-wide search. His friends Mike, Lucas, and Dustin hide Eleven, a girl with psychokinetic powers who has escaped the Hawkins Laboratory, hoping she can help find him.

title: Premiere of Stranger Things
phrase: the premiere of Stranger Things
description: The Duffer Brothers pitched it to about 15 cable networks, all of which said a show led by kids wouldn't work and asked them to make it a children's series or drop the children. Netflix, newly known for House of Cards and Orange Is the New Black, gave them a chance. It was first called Montauk and set on Long Island before moving to Hawkins, Indiana.

title: Release of Stranger Things season 2
phrase: the release of Stranger Things season 2
description: Out just before Halloween and set in Halloween season 1984, a year after Will Byers came back from the Upside Down. Something is rotting the town's pumpkin patches, and Will keeps seeing a giant many-armed shadow the party names the Mind Flayer.

title: Release of Stranger Things season 3
phrase: the release of Stranger Things season 3
description: Released on the Fourth of July and set in the summer of 1985, when the new Starcourt Mall is closing Hawkins' other stores. The mall was the re-dressed Gwinnett Place Mall in Georgia, a dead mall built in 1984, with Steve scooping ice cream at the fictional Scoops Ahoy.

title: Release of Stranger Things season 4
phrase: the release of Stranger Things season 4
description: The longest season yet, so Netflix split it: seven episodes in May and the last two on July 1. The villain, Vecna, is named after the Dungeons & Dragons character, and Max escapes him to Kate Bush's "Running Up That Hill," which sent the 1985 song back up the charts.

title: Release of Stranger Things season 5
phrase: the release of Stranger Things season 5
description: The final season came in three drops: four episodes on November 26, three on Christmas, and the finale on New Year's Eve. Netflix added 30% more bandwidth for the premiere, and the site crashed anyway.

title: Stranger Things series finale
phrase: the Stranger Things series finale
description: The finale streamed on Netflix and played in 620 theaters in the US and Canada, from New Year's Eve into New Year's Day. Because of the cast's residuals contracts, the 1.1 million tickets sold in advance were technically concession vouchers. Netflix crashed again shortly after it aired.

title: Premiere of Star Trek
phrase: the premiere of Star Trek
description: Gene Roddenberry pitched it as "Wagon Train to the stars." NBC turned down the first pilot as "too cerebral" and, unusually, paid for a second one. Ratings were low and NBC canceled it after 79 episodes, but reruns in syndication made it a hit in the 1970s.

title: Kirk and Uhura kiss on Star Trek
phrase: Kirk and Uhura's kiss on Star Trek
description: In "Plato's Stepchildren," William Shatner's Kirk kissed Nichelle Nichols's Uhura, one of the earliest kisses between a white man and a Black woman on US television, though not the first. NBC worried about stations in the Deep South, but Nichols said the fan mail was huge and almost none of it objected.

title: Premiere of Star Trek: The Next Generation
phrase: the premiere of Star Trek: The Next Generation
description: The networks would only consider pilot scripts or a miniseries, so Paramount sold it directly to individual stations in first-run syndication. Patrick Stewart's Captain Picard commanded the Enterprise-D for 178 episodes over seven seasons, then four movies.

title: Premiere of Star Trek: Deep Space Nine
phrase: the premiere of Star Trek: Deep Space Nine
description: The first Star Trek set on a space station instead of a starship, and the first led by an African American: Avery Brooks as Benjamin Sisko. The station orbits Bajor, whose people have just thrown off a long Cardassian occupation, and sits beside a wormhole to the far side of the galaxy.

title: Premiere of Star Trek: Voyager
phrase: the premiere of Star Trek: Voyager
description: The first Star Trek with a woman in command as its lead: Kate Mulgrew as Captain Kathryn Janeway, stranded with her crew on the far side of the galaxy. It was the first show on UPN, the new network Paramount wanted it to launch.
